proof:
Source: step 13 of the parent proof (testing ∂T = 0 with φ = (η∘Q)·Pr^#ψ). Sibling lemma used (as the frozen declaration Submission.dgcr_orthogonal_coordinates): DEC.
Notation used throughout: ℝ^m means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); e₁, …, eₙ (0-indexed below as e₀, …, eₙ₋₁, Lean EuclideanSpace.single i 1, i : Fin n) is the standard basis of ℝⁿ; ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} are linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w; ι*, ι'* are their adjoints; D := B_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (open ball); Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v); Pr(x) := ι*(x − z), Q(x) := ι'*(x − z); DΦ(v) := fderiv ℝ Φ v and b(v) := (DΦ(v)e₀, …, DΦ(v)eₙ₋₁); C := {z + ιv + ι'w : ‖v‖ < s, ‖w‖ < h}; ∂ⱼa(v) := Da(v)eⱼ (fderiv ℝ a v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)). The library exterior derivative is Mathlib's extDeriv (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative), with dω(x)(w₀, …, w_m) = Σᵢ (−1)^i·D[y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth i w)](x)(wᵢ) for ω differentiable at x (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative_apply).
Formalization note: unless this child is split further it is a machine leaf (one theorem appended to the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, no new import or helper declaration); the accepted sibling declaration is merged into its base; all library lemmas cited are in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission (ContDiffBump on Euclid k uses the inner-product-space instance hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace).
0. Write n = m + 1 (0 < n; obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_one_of_ne_zero). For n = m + 1, BoundaryVanishes T unfolds to T.boundary = 0, i.e. T(dφ) = T.boundary φ = 0 for every φ ∈ TestFormOn U m (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply; the form underlying exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m φ is exteriorDerivative φ). Adjoint identities: ι*ι = id, ι*ι' = 0, ι'*ι' = id, ι'*ι = 0 (since ι is an isometry, ⟨ι*ιv, v'⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιv'⟩ = ⟨v, v'⟩ for all v'; by orthogonality ⟨ι*ι'w, v'⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιv'⟩ = 0 for all v'; symmetrically for ι'); hence Pr(Φ(v)) = v, Q(Φ(v)) = u(v), and, for v ∈ D, DΦ(v) = ι + ι'∘Du(v) (u is differentiable on the open set D), so ι*(DΦ(v)eᵢ) = eᵢ. By DEC(a) (applied to x − z) and the adjoint identities, every x equals z + ι(Pr x) + ι'(Q x).
1. Fix a ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with compact support and K_a := tsupport a ⊆ D, and fix j. K_a is compact and u is continuous on D ⊇ K_a, so u(K_a) is a compact subset of B_h(0) (hypothesis u(D) ⊆ B_h(0)); choose h₂ with max_{K_a}‖u‖ < h₂ < h (h₂ := h/2 if K_a = ∅; otherwise the maximum is attained, IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn). Choose η ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^k) with η ≡ 1 on B̄_{h₂}(0) and K_η := tsupport η ⊆ B_h(0): a ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = h₂ and rOut = (h₂ + h)/2 (ContDiffBump.contDiff, ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall, ContDiffBump.tsupport_eq).
2. The constant m-covector βⱼ on ℝⁿ: βⱼ(w₁, …, w_m) := δ(eⱼ, w₁, …, w_m), where δ is the standard determinant n-form on ℝⁿ: the basis determinant (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det made into a continuous alternating map (e.g. AlternatingMap.mkContinuous with the Leibniz bound |δ(c)| ≤ (card of the permutation group)·∏ᵢ‖cᵢ‖, or continuity of c ↦ det of its coordinate matrix via Continuous.matrix_det; automatic continuity MultilinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional is not in the import closure), with δ(e₀, …, eₙ₋₁) = 1; βⱼ is ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft δ applied to eⱼ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply). For i ∈ Fin n, βⱼ applied to (e₀, …, eₙ₋₁) with eᵢ removed (Fin.removeNth i e) equals 0 if i ≠ j (eⱼ then occurs twice in (eⱼ, removeNth i e), and an alternating map vanishes on families with a repeated vector, AlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq) and equals (−1)^j if i = j (moving eⱼ from the first slot to slot j is a cycle of length j + 1: Fin.cons_removeNth_eq_comp_cycleRange_symm writes (eⱼ, removeNth j e) as e ∘ (cycleRange j)⁻¹, the determinant form changes by the sign of this permutation (AlternatingMap.map_perm), Equiv.Perm.sign_symm and Fin.sign_cycleRange give sign (−1)^j, and δ(e) = 1, Module.Basis.det_self).
3. ψ := a·βⱼ is a smooth m-form on ℝⁿ with tsupport ψ ⊆ K_a. By the expansion of the exterior derivative recalled in the notation paragraph (exteriorDerivative_apply, applicable since ψ is differentiable) and since the scalar function y ↦ ψ(y)(removeNth i w) = a(y)·βⱼ(removeNth i w) has derivative (Da(x)wᵢ)·βⱼ(removeNth i w) in the direction wᵢ, step 2 gives dψ(x)(e₀, …, eₙ₋₁) = Σᵢ (−1)^i ∂ᵢa(x)·βⱼ(removeNth i e) = (−1)^j·∂ⱼa(x)·(−1)^j = ∂ⱼa(x) for every x ∈ ℝⁿ.
4. Pull-back. Let P^#ψ := affinePullbackForm ι* (−ι*z) ψ, i.e. (P^#ψ)(x)(w₁, …, w_m) = ψ(Pr x)(ι*w₁, …, ι*w_m) (because −ι*z + ι*x = Pr x). It is smooth (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm) and d(P^#ψ) = P^#(dψ) (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm), i.e. d(P^#ψ)(x)(w₀, …, w_m) = dψ(Pr x)(ι*w₀, …, ι*w_m).
5. The test form φ(x) := η(Q x)·(P^#ψ)(x) is smooth (η∘Q is smooth since Q is affine; product of a smooth scalar function and a smooth form). If φ(x) ≠ 0 then Q x ∈ support η and Pr x ∈ support a, so tsupport φ ⊆ S := {x : Pr x ∈ K_a, Q x ∈ K_η} (a closed set). By step 0, S = {z + ιv + ι'w : v ∈ K_a, w ∈ K_η}, the image of the compact set K_a × K_η under the continuous map (v, w) ↦ z + ιv + ι'w, hence compact; and S ⊆ C ⊆ U because K_a ⊆ B_s(0) and K_η ⊆ B_h(0). So φ ∈ TestFormOn U m (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ U), and tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ C (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset).
6. Pointwise identity: for v ∈ D, dφ(Φ(v))(b(v)) = ∂ⱼa(v).
 (i) If v ∈ K_a: ‖Q Φ(v)‖ = ‖u(v)‖ < h₂, so O := {x : ‖Q x‖ < h₂} is an open neighbourhood of Φ(v) on which η∘Q ≡ 1, i.e. φ = P^#ψ on O. The exterior derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the form (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq; it is built from fderiv), so dφ(Φ(v)) = d(P^#ψ)(Φ(v)) = (P^#dψ)(Φ(v)), and by steps 0, 3 and 4: dφ(Φ(v))(b(v)) = dψ(v)(ι*b₀(v), …, ι*bₙ₋₁(v)) = dψ(v)(e₀, …, eₙ₋₁) = ∂ⱼa(v).
 (ii) If v ∈ D ∖ K_a: O' := {x : Pr x ∉ K_a} is open (K_a is closed), contains Φ(v) (Pr Φ(v) = v), and φ ≡ 0 on O' (a(Pr x) = 0 there). Hence dφ(Φ(v)) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq comparing φ with the zero form, whose exterior derivative is 0, e.g. via exteriorDerivative_smul 0); also ∂ⱼa(v) = 0 since v ∉ tsupport a (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport). Both sides vanish.
7. Apply the representation hypothesis to ω := dφ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m φ ∈ TestFormOn U n (tsupport ⊆ C by step 5): 0 = T(dφ) = ∫_D G(v)·dφ(Φ(v))(b(v)) dv = ∫_D G(v)·∂ⱼa(v) dv, the last equality by step 6 (setIntegral_congr_fun on the measurable set D). ∎

ψ := a·βⱼ with βⱼ = δ(eⱼ, ·) has dψ(x)(e₀, …, eₙ₋₁) = ∂ⱼa(x) under Mathlib's extDeriv convention (cycleRange sign (−1)^j twice).
φ := (η∘Q)·Pr^#ψ is a test form with compact support in C (DEC), and d(Pr^#ψ) = Pr^#dψ.
dφ(Φ(v))(DΦ(v)e) = ∂ⱼa(v) on D (germ argument using η∘Q ≡ 1 near the graph over spt a, φ ≡ 0 elsewhere, and ι*DΦ(v) = id).
The representation of T on C applied to dφ gives ∫_D G ∂ⱼa = 0.
